# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 2 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 2
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. The days are evil, and the evil one himself holds power in this present age. So we need to be watchful and to search out the Lord's righteous requirements.
2. The foundations of our faith are fear and patience; our partners are endurance and self-control.
3. When these are kept pure in relation to the Lord, wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and insight thrive alongside them.
4. Through all the prophets God has made it unmistakably clear that he does not need sacrifices, burnt offerings, or general gifts. In one place he says:
5. "What do I care about all your sacrifices?" says the Lord. "I have had more than enough of burnt rams and the fat of well-fed lambs. I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls and goats — not even when you show up to stand before me. Who asked you for any of this?
6. Stop trampling my courts. Your grain offerings are pointless; your incense stinks to me. I cannot stand your new moons and your sabbaths.
7. He has cancelled all these things so that the new law of our Lord Jesus Christ — without any yoke of coercion — might receive its human offering.
8. He also says to them: "When I brought your fathers out of Egypt, did I command them to bring me burnt offerings and sacrifices?
9. No — here is what I commanded them: None of you is to hold a grudge against a neighbor, and do not swear by a false oath."
10. If we have any wisdom at all, we should understand what our Father's kindness is actually pointing toward. He speaks to us because he wants us not to follow their mistake of trying to figure out what kind of gifts to bring him.
11. To us he says this instead: "A broken heart is a sacrifice to God; a heart that glorifies its Maker is a sweet fragrance to the Lord." Brothers, we must be on guard for our salvation — the evil one might sneak error in through the side door and knock us away from the life we have.
